correctness.rationale: The matrix-coordinate reduction is valid in characteristic two and identifies the commuting relation with three minors. A generating additive character exists for every finite commutative chain ring. Primitive-vector stratification and exact hyperplane annihilators produce the complete Smith-stratum multiplier, whose negative boundary and positive branches exclude further zeros. Fourier support is the lift of the lower-length determinantal variety; direct counting gives the stated rank. Exact canonical cyclotomic and all-noncyclic Walsh computations passed, alongside transform-wide cyclic checks. Finite computations are supplementary, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Košir–Sethuraman study the identical determinantal congruence as a geometric variety, but not the Fourier transform of the commuting-pair indicator. Browning–Sawin–Wang explicitly study commuting-pair exponential sums modulo a prime but only state estimates in the inspected §3–4. Britnell–Wildon classify commuting similarity classes over finite fields. Direct published-record queries and accessible earlier related statements yielded no theorem implying the all-chain-ring one-length Fourier-support descent and exact convolution-rank polynomial. The inference is bounded; the existence of a stronger matrix-association-scheme formulation is a genuine risk.
residual_risks: A historical formula for the Fourier eigenmatrix of Smith-rank association schemes over finite chain rings might imply this specialization, despite lacking exact matching keywords.
The published commuting integer matrix paper has additional sections not completely inspected; its directly relevant Fourier-sum section was checked.
No independent expert originality review has been conducted.

value.rationale: Commuting matrix pairs form a canonical incidence variety. Their additive convolution kernel is a natural invariant not fixed by geometric dimension or point counts. The precise one-ring-length dual determinantal condition and uniform rank polynomial for all chain rings exhibit a structural descent principle, a characteristic-independent law, and exponentially thinning Fourier support at higher lengths, giving a useful spectral classification rather than a routine one-off count.
